content.label: Stated goal, rules and rollout
content.takeaway: What the proposal commits to in plain words.

nodes.title: One pipeline instead of three logging tools

content.markdown: A single pipeline should collect, enrich and land product-analytics events in the warehouse, so the growth team can answer funnel questions (how many new accounts finish onboarding, which features paying customers use in their first month) without exporting CSV files by hand.

nodes.title: Privacy: no emails or free text, IPs truncated

content.markdown: Events must not contain email addresses or free-text input from users. The collector truncates IP addresses before an event is published.

nodes.title: Not for monitoring, not a revenue record

content.markdown: Not meant for operational monitoring or alerting (logs and metrics stay in the observability stack), and not a replacement for the billing system's revenue records.

nodes.title: Phase 1: web sign-up and checkout events

content.markdown: About 6 weeks for 2 engineers. The proposal asks for approval to start phase 1 while the open questions are settled in parallel.

content.label: Open questions and conflicts
content.takeaway: Contradictions and gaps to settle before building; nothing here is decided.

nodes.title: How fresh is the warehouse? The proposal says two things

content.markdown:
The design section says enriched events are written to the warehouse in **hourly batches**; the freshness section says events reach the warehouse **in real time**. The proposal doesn't say which is meant.

It matters: product managers want adoption data during launches, and launch reviews happen within 2 hours of a release.

nodes.title: How long are raw events kept? The proposal gives two values

content.markdown: The retention section says raw events are kept for **30 days**; the components table says **90 days** for warehouse raw events. The proposal doesn't say which is meant.
Not decided: neither the platform team nor the data team owns the registry yet; each has suggested the other. The components table lists the owner as TBD.

nodes.title: How does enrichment use the user service?

content.markdown: The proposal only says enrichment "uses" it. A call per event, a cached lookup and a read from a replica all fit the text; which one is not stated. The user service should stay lightly loaded, which argues against a call per event but doesn't settle it.

- Aggregate-table retention: TBD.
- Rejected events: dropped, or kept for debugging?
- Running cost: not estimated.
- Phase 2 (mobile): waits for the mobile SDK; no date set.
- Mobile events: same schemas as web?
